levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Some criteria are used and others are dropped without saying why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: Every stated criterion is applied and the result of each is reported.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: Every criterion is applied and the response says which one decided the outcome.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

judgment.prompt: The employer contribution is larger in dollars, and the card balance is the more urgent problem in other ways. Explain why comparing 100% with 19.2% directly is a mistake, and describe an allocation of $300 a month across the two claims that you could defend, naming what it gives up.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains why the percentages are not comparable: 100% is a one-time addition to money contributed, while 19.2% is a rate charged every year the balance is carried, so the two describe different things and only a dollar figure over a stated period compares them.
Proposes a specific allocation of the $300 with figures — for example $152.00 to secure the full employer contribution and $148.00 to the card — and shows the parts summing to $300.
Names what the allocation gives up: a slower reduction in the $2,900 balance, or a smaller employer contribution than the $1,824.00 available.
Recognises that the $556.80 figure assumes the balance stays put, so paying it down reduces the charge as well as the balance.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $1,824.00 annual employer contribution and the $556.80 annual interest, and shows an allocation summing to $300.
lookFors: The response converts both claims to dollars before ranking them.
More than one allocation is defensible and each is credited when the sacrifice is named.
The response does not present a course of action as advice for a real person.
judgment.commonMisconception: Ranking a matching rate against an interest rate by comparing the two percentages, when one applies once to contributions and the other applies annually to a balance.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
